title: DX Initiative — SDK Quickstarts Flywheel & Signal Harmonization
creator: Maya Chen
description: Objective: Build a repeatable flywheel that converts first-time SDK users into active customers through opinionated quickstarts, targeted micro-docs, and telemetry-driven iteration. This initiative bundles content work, sample app engineering, and a lightweight signals contract so product and engineering can run continuous experiments during the 2025 Q4 developer growth push. Scope: 1) 4 reference quickstarts (Node, Python, Java, cURL) with end-to-end sample apps, 2) 6 microlearning snippets keyed to common DX failure modes, 3) telemetry contract + dashboard to track funnel conversion and time-to-first-success, 4) onboarding PRD and rollout checklist for SDK teams.
acceptance_criteria: Four quickstarts published in the docs site with working sample apps and CI that validates smoke scenarios
Telemetry contract implemented: events for quickstart_start, quickstart_complete, sample_app_run, first_api_call_success
Dashboard shows baseline funnel (visit -> start -> complete -> first_success) and can be filtered by SDK/runtime
OKR: Improve time-to-first-success by 30% for new SDK users (measured by median time in dashboard)
Playbook and rollout checklist reviewed and signed off by DX and Engineering leads
notes: Trade-offs: we chose to prioritize Node and Python sample apps for deeper UX polish; Java and cURL will be scaffolded with minimal polish in cycle 1 to accelerate delivery.
Telemetry design uses lightweight event payloads to avoid PII; we will pair with Security on event schema to confirm no sensitive data is captured.
Decision log: Use feature-flagged rollout for quickstarts to enable canary exposure and allow fast rollback if telemetry shows regressions.
Risk: sample app maintenance overhead — propose adding a biweekly rotation task to eng on-call to keep examples aligned with SDK releases.
